props.title:
Indian Auto Stocks
Tyres, Rubber & Batteries
props.sub: 14 companies · what they do · latest quarter · P/E · their moat

props.title: The Tyre Makers
props.sub: Where a rubber-price shock just bit hard

props.name: MRF
biz: India's largest tyre maker — and its priciest listed share
Tyres for everything from two-wheelers to aircraft
Also paints, conveyor belts and toys

fin.note: Margins held up better than peers despite the cost spike.

props.moat: The strongest brand in Indian tyres — scale, disciplined pricing and leadership in premium replacement.

props.name: Apollo Tyres
biz: Cars, trucks, two-wheelers and farm tyres
Apollo brand in India, premium Vredestein in Europe
Plants across India and Europe

fin.note: Profit jumped off a weak base; a new CFO takes over.

props.moat: A strong Indian brand plus European premium tyres (Vredestein) — the cheapest valuation of the majors.

props.name: Balkrishna Industries (BKT)
biz: Specialist in off-highway tyres — agriculture, mining, construction
Sells largely into export replacement markets abroad
A niche exporter, not an on-road tyre maker

fin.note: EBITDA margin a fat 21.5% — the star of the quarter.

props.moat: A low-cost specialist in a niche global market — roughly 6% of world off-highway tyres, with rich margins.

props.name: CEAT
biz: RPG-group tyre maker
Strong in two-wheeler and truck-bus tyres
OEM, replacement and exports

fin.note: Profit crashed 96% as rubber and crude costs spiked.

props.moat: A solid two-wheeler and truck-bus replacement brand — but a price-taker on rubber, so margins swing hard.

props.name: JK Tyre & Industries
biz: A pioneer of radial tyres in India
Trucks, buses, cars and off-highway
Plants in India and Mexico

fin.note: Same cost squeeze — but domestic volumes still rose 25%.

props.moat: Strength in truck radials plus scale — but leveraged and cyclical, so profits swing with input costs.

props.name: Goodyear India
biz: The Indian arm of America's Goodyear
Mainly farm/tractor and passenger-car tyres
OEM and replacement markets

fin.note: A small, steady player focused on the tractor-tyre niche.

props.moat: A global brand and a farm-tyre niche — but small, and licensing-linked to its US parent.

props.name: TVS Srichakra
biz: TVS-group maker of two- and three-wheeler tyres
Sold under the TVS Eurogrip brand
Plus off-highway and specialty tyres

fin.note: Thin margins — the rubber cost spike bites small makers too.

props.moat: A focused two-wheeler-tyre brand inside the TVS ecosystem — but margin-sensitive to rubber prices.

props.title: Rubber & Recycling
props.sub: Retreading, crumb rubber and old names

props.name: Tinna Rubber & Infrastructure
biz: Recycles end-of-life tyres into crumb rubber
Makes crumb-rubber-modified bitumen for roads
A play on sustainability and the circular economy

fin.note: Small but profitable, riding an ESG and road-building tailwind.

props.moat: A first-mover leader in the growing tyre-recycling niche — scale plus a sustainability tailwind.

props.name: Elgi Rubber
biz: Tyre-retreading materials and rubber machinery
Reclaimed rubber and rubber products
Operates across the global retreading chain
props.moat: A niche in retreading and rubber recycling — but sub-scale and often unprofitable.

props.name: Tolins Tyres
biz: A Kerala-based maker of tyres and tubes
Plus precured tread rubber and compounds
Sells in domestic and export markets
props.moat: A small regional maker across the tyre and retread chain — limited scale, limited edge.

props.name: Modi Rubber
biz: Once a well-known tyre brand under the Modi group
Core tyre operations have shrunk sharply
Now largely investment and asset interests

fin.note: The tyre business is a shadow of its past; recent quarter in the red.

props.moat: None operationally — whatever value exists is in legacy assets and investments, not tyres.

props.name: PTL Enterprises
biz: Owns the Kerala tyre plant leased to Apollo Tyres
Earns steady lease income from it
Also has healthcare interests via Artemis
props.moat: Stable, annuity-style lease income — low risk, but a holding-type entity tied to the Apollo promoter group.

props.title: The Battery Duopoly
props.sub: Exide vs Amara Raja — and the lithium bet

props.name: Exide Industries
biz: India's largest lead-acid battery maker
Car, two-wheeler, inverter and industrial batteries
Building a lithium-ion cell gigafactory for EVs

fin.note: A solid quarter; margins expanding as it invests in lithium.

props.moat: Number one in a battery duopoly — brand, nationwide distribution and steady replacement demand, plus a lithium bet.

props.name: Amara Raja Energy & Mobility
biz: The Amaron and PowerZone battery maker
The number two in the lead-acid duopoly
Pushing into lithium cells, chargers and EV packs

fin.note: Q1 FY27 lands around 11-Aug; figures shown are the prior quarter.

props.moat: The strong number two in the battery duopoly — Amaron brand and distribution, plus a new-energy push.

props.title: Tyres, Rubber & Batteries — in one breath
items: A rubber & crude cost spike crushed tyre profits this quarter
CEAT −96% and JK Tyre −73% — margins are the whole story
MRF and Apollo, the strongest brands, held up best
Balkrishna (BKT) shone — a niche off-highway export moat
Tinna recycles tyres; the legacy names have faded
Exide & Amara Raja: a two-player battery market, now betting on lithium
Watch input costs — they decide tyre earnings quarter to quarter
props.closer: In tyres, brand and cost control are everything — and in batteries, it's a cosy club of two.
